decision: The .xpi of the ClearURLs add-on, installed through the browser's own add-on installation (browser_extension action via the browser's remote protocol). The browser counts as an installer in that part (S8.1-5), the add-on is what it installs and removes as a whole (S8.1-6): Q1, an installed object; S8.2-1: must be recorded, by a line of its own (S8.2-16). S8.2-21: code that runs inside a recorded program (the browser package) and cannot itself launch programs or change what is installed and the computer's settings need not be recorded. If the add-on can do neither, S8.2-1 and S8.2-21 decide in opposite ways, and S8.2-6 only fixes the order of the questions, not which of the two prevails. FACT_UNKNOWN: the add-on's permissions (the .xpi content is not in the inventory); if it can launch programs or change settings, Q1 and S8.2-1 decide alone.
meaning_answer: yes, by a line of its own
achievable: yes: the browser's installer can add the add-on to the declaration as it installs it (the mechanism is outside the definition, 8.5); installing an extension stays allowed

decision: Members that bash executes as code at start-up or logout (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .bash_logout): code by S8.2-23, Q2 program, not obtained as received with a package (Q1 no), so a line of its own. .bash_history: two-ways. Read by S8.2-9 it is code the computer can execute at a person's command (shell statements that bash replays with fc or !n, or runs as a script): a program, line of its own. Read by S8.2-23 bash only reads the file as values into its history list: not code, Q3 no, Q4 'history' named in S8.2-15: program record, need not be recorded. Nothing says which reading prevails. actions-status.tsv: written by the action runner as it ran, Q4 program record. Subdirectories (.bun, .cache, .config, .julia, .juliaup, .local, .ssh, Projects, actions-logs, bin) are separate objects.
meaning_answer: yes by lines of their own for the shell start-up files; no for .bash_history and actions-status.tsv
achievable: yes: start-up files can be files of the declaration itself (S8.1-3 lets a person designate them); history and logs need nothing
